correctness.rationale: Independent finite replay generated normalized points and covectors, took all submasks of line complements, and reduced the augmented oriented boundary matrices by sparse integer cross-multiplication over Q (not Morse matching). The ranks for maps out of degrees 0 through 8 were 1,12,66,220,482,649,364,104,13; the only nonzero reduced Betti numbers were 39 in degree 4 and 1 in degree 5. Every projective class has a unique determinant-one representative over F_3. SL_3(F_3) is generated by elementary transvections, each a commutator using the third index, hence perfect; degree 5 is therefore trivial. Independently enumerated all 5616 determinant-one matrices and distinct permutations. Summed over their cycle unions that were faces: a nonempty union of r cycles contributes (−1)^(r−1), with augmentation −1. Adding back the trivial degree-five character gave exactly all eight (cycle type, count, trace) rows; the trace sum was 0 and the square sum 5616, proving absolute irreducibility in characteristic zero and no degree-four invariants. Replay: python3 /workspace/branches/review-2-replay.py.
residual_risks: The independent chain computation is over Q, not a Smith normal form or an equivariant homotopy certificate. The rational Finding does not require those stronger conclusions.

evidence: The point-side neighborhood complex of the nonincidence graph is K. The later line-avoidance complex X has faces containing no full line, equivalently those whose complements meet every line: X=K*. Its degree-six character table matches every row of the reviewed degree-four table.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: On 13 points, equivariant combinatorial Alexander duality relates degrees i and 10−i by cohomological duality and the vertex-permutation sign. Here the sign is trivial by perfectness and the rational character is invariant under inversion. Thus the later table is mathematically equivalent coverage of the degree-four action; it is not evidence of an earlier source. The earlier same-object statement is nonequivariant.

value.rationale: A natural invariant of the smallest projective plane in this comparison with mixed-dimensional neighborhood homology is how its large symmetry group acts on those different degrees. The result identifies an irreducible homology realization and proves that the 39-dimensional layer contributes no collineation invariants while the fifth does. This is useful for equivariant comparisons and fixed-class questions; it is not merely enumeration of an abstract existing character table or a repeat of the homology rank computation.
residual_risks: No general theorem for all projective planes or assertion about the integral representation lattice is credited.
